solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Banger's essential part is a custom on 5th of November to take in

parts.note: the contraction 's stands for is
a usage is a custom or habitual practice

indicators.note: the fifth letter of the following word is taken, counting N-O-V-E-M

parts.note: to take in food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A sausage, and the habit of letting off bangers on Bonfire Night, 5th November, when Guy Fawkes is remembered in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' is British slang for a sausage, though the surface points to a firework.
explanation.definitionFit: The filling of a sausage, its essential part, is minced meat prepared for stuffing into skins.

clue.text: Scotsman's no good in Australia

indicators.note: the letters for no good are placed inside the abbreviation for Australia

explanation.surface: A Scot who emigrated has proved useless Down Under.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus is a typical Scottish male name, so it stands for a Scotsman by example.

clue.text: Instruction to look elsewhere in document for leak

definitions.text: Instruction to look elsewhere in document
definitions.meaning: a cross-reference telling the reader to turn to another page, written as two words
a slow escape of liquid through small openings

explanation.surface: A cross-reference in a report pointing to where a leak is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid oozing out slowly through a crack is a classic escape or leak, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Knight to run faster to embrace a woman

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the next pieces go within the word for run faster

parts.note: to gain on someone is to run faster than them

explanation.surface: A knight sprints ahead to hug a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain is one of the knights of King Arthur's Round Table, an example of a knight.

clue.text: A gremlin contrived to throw a sickie

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially put together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mischievous gremlin arranged things so someone could skip work feigning illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw a sickie' is British and Australian slang for taking a day off work pretending to be ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigning illness to avoid duty is exactly what shirking by faking sickness amounts to.

clue.text: Bad digestion encourages one to enter Alcoholics Anonymous

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so these pieces sit within the abbreviation

parts.note: peps (up) means encourages or invigorates
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone with stomach trouble urges a friend to join Alcoholics Anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for indigestion, the failure of the stomach to process food properly.

clue.text: Hostile Indian continent named by explorers as a dystopia

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior
the Americas were called the New World by European explorers

explanation.surface: Explorers name an untamed land after its warriors, picturing a nightmarish society.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Huxley's novel of that name depicts a controlled future society, the classic literary dystopia.

clue.text: One gets wind about case where justice is not done

definitions.text: case where justice is not done

indicators.note: the wind's letters go round the piece for one

parts.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind in southern France
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone catches wind of a legal case that went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial voided by an error in procedure, so no proper verdict or justice results.

clue.text: Asteroid often crashed clearing a lot of trees

indicators.note: something crashed is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An asteroid that often crashes into land flattens whole forests.
explanation.definitionFit: The felling of a forest over a wide area is the process of stripping land of woodland.

clue.text: Rascal with Irish accent not British

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for British is dropped

parts.note: a brogue is a strong Irish accent

explanation.surface: A rogue who talks with an Irish lilt rather than an English one.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel or mischievous person; the two words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Beast makes person like you lose head in drink

indicators.note: the shortened piece is placed inside the word for drink

parts.note: wine is a drink

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the reader of a crossword is a solver

explanation.surface: A boozy solver loses their head and turns into an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose head' takes the S off SOLVER, leaving OLVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce carnivorous mammal of northern forests, the largest of the weasel family, is a beast.

clue.text: He ruled all the Mediterranean region save Spain, surprisingly

definitions.text: He ruled all the Mediterranean region

indicators.note: a surprising result is an unexpected arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A ruler who held the whole Mediterranean except Spain, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespasian was a Roman emperor, so his rule covered the lands around the whole Mediterranean.

clue.text: Hottest wingers going back to start

indicators.note: back means the remaining letters are read in the opposite direction
the wingers are the letters at each end, and they leave

explanation.surface: The fastest wide players run back to the kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingers going' leaves OTTES, and 'back' turns it to give SETTO, read as the phrase 'set to'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set to is to begin working vigorously, so the phrase means to start.

clue.text: Nationalist, say, crazy guy

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A nationalist, for example, dismissed as a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an eccentric or deranged person, a madman.

clue.text: Long book about artists' materials is hard going

indicators.note: the book's letters go round the artists' materials

parts.note: a tome is a large, heavy book
oils are oil paints used by artists

explanation.surface: A long book about painting materials proves a difficult read.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laborious and demanding much effort is arduous or hard going.

clue.text: This land's uncultivated even at Wimbledon

definitions.meaning: farmland deliberately left fallow under an agricultural scheme
in tennis, a set apiece leaves the players level

explanation.surface: Fallow land, even at the home of the tennis championships.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London home of the grass-court tennis championships; read as 'set a side', each player has won one set.
explanation.definitionFit: EU farm policy paid farmers to leave fields out of production, called by this name.

clue.text: Bird — pluck and consume it, finally tucking in

indicators.note: tucking in means the other pieces are put inside the word for pluck

parts.note: grit and pluck both mean courage
to consume food is to eat it

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing a bird: pluck it and eat it, finally getting stuck in.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European songbird, the largest of the tits, is a bird by example.

clue.text: 18th-century politics with hour for start of greed

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for greed is replaced, signalled by 'for start of'

parts.note: piggery can mean greediness, behaving like a pig

explanation.surface: Eighteenth-century political life came with time set aside for greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hour' gives H, which replaces the P of PIGGERY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whigs were the dominant party in 18th-century Britain, and the word means their principles.

clue.text: Secret police disrupted postage

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Secret police interfering with the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi state's secret police force, the archetype of such an organisation.

clue.text: Cat in patch of ground by old church

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
a lot is a plot or patch of land

explanation.surface: A cat prowls in a small plot beside an ancient church.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotted wild feline of Central and South America, an example of a cat.

clue.text: Cat that's sharp spoken

indicators.note: spoken signals the word is heard rather than read, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a sharp, or sharper, is a swindler or cheater

explanation.surface: A cat with a cutting voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest land animal is a large spotted wild feline, an example of a cat.

clue.text: Indian espousing simple life has ingredients for ghi

wordplay.reading: the letters of GHI split as G, HI

parts.note: the letters making up the word ghi are the letter G together with the pair HI

explanation.surface: An ascetic Indian who keeps a simple diet including clarified butter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ghi (or ghee) is clarified butter used in Indian cooking; the clue spells its letters as 'G and HI'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi, India's independence leader, famously lived austerely, spinning his own cloth.

clue.text: Rock band over in present form

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
as is means in the current condition, unchanged

explanation.surface: A rock group, finished, preserved in its current line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manchester group led by the Gallagher brothers is an example of a rock band.

clue.text: A place down under is humbling

parts.note: a basement is a room below ground level

explanation.surface: Being sent to a spot in Australia is humiliating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' suggests Australia but just means below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun sense of humbling, a lowering of someone's dignity or status.

clue.text: Spooky Oriental lake

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
Lake Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: An eerie lake in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and frightening in a ghostly way, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Criticised having kept going without a doctor

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for kept going surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: lasted means continued or kept going
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Criticised for keeping on working with no medical help.
explanation.definitionFit: To be harshly attacked verbally, scolded or berated.

clue.text: Trunk is one end of elephant, roughly speaking

indicators.note: one end here means the last letter of the following word

parts.note: 'or so' means approximately

explanation.surface: An elephant's trunk is at one end, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' pretends to belong to the elephant but means the body's middle part.
explanation.definitionFit: The human body without head or limbs is called the trunk.

clue.text: Almost went mad, one in endless torment in Cornwall

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: lost one's wits means went mad

indicators.note: the letter for one is put inside the shortened torment
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: hell is torment
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone nearly driven mad by never-ending suffering while in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-west tip. 'Almost' drops the S of LOSTWITS; 'endless' cuts HELL to HEL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small historic town in the county, once its capital, so it is a place there.
